title: Several lines and a legend
summary: Compare cities on one chart: each ax.plot() adds a line, label= names it and ax.legend() lists the names. A loop over the columns draws one line per city, however many the file has. Markers and line styles help when the chart is printed in grey.
objectives: Draw several series on one axes.
Name each with label= and show them with legend().
Loop over a table’s columns to draw one line each.
Use markers and line styles so lines can be told apart.

slides.h: By the end: three cities, one chart
slides.say: temps.csv has the average temperature each month for three cities, one column per city. Three lines on one chart show at once which city is hottest, and when.
points: Each `ax.plot(...)` adds a line to the same axes.
`ax.legend()` draws the list of names and colours.
p: temps.csv has the average temperature each month for three cities, one column per city. Three lines on one chart show at once which city is hottest, and when.
Each `ax.plot(...)` adds a line to the same axes.
`ax.legend()` draws the list of names and colours.

visual.text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
df = pd.read_csv("temps.csv")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
for city in df.columns[1:]:
    ax.plot(df["Month"], df[city], label=city)
ax.legend()
ax.set_ylabel("Temperature (°C)")

terms: one set of values drawn together: one line, or one set of bars
the key that says which colour is which series

slides.say: `df.columns[1:]` is every column name after Month. Looping over it draws one line per city, so a file with two cities or ten works with the same code.
points: `for city in df.columns[1:]:` skips the Month column.
`df[city]` is that city’s column; `label=city` names it.

visual.text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
df = pd.read_csv("temps.csv")
plt.plot(df["Month"], df["Sundarpur"], marker="o", label="Sundarpur")
plt.plot(df["Month"], df["Meghpur"], linestyle="--", label="Meghpur")
plt.legend()
plt.ylabel("Temperature (°C)")
